newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police say no bomb in car at British base.
newsitem.headline: German police say no bomb in car at British base.

text.p: German police said on Wednesday they had found no bomb in a stolen car near a British barracks, and said a bomb alert leading to the evacuation of hundreds of people from their homes had been a false alarm.
Bomb experts searched the car, standing in a residential street near the British air force barracks in the North Rhine-Westphalian town of Niederkruechten, for several hours.
"It was a false alarm by British explosives experts," local police spokesman Wilhelm Schnitzler told Reuters.

The car, with British number plates, was registered as stolen on March 24 and noticed by military officers patrolling the residential area near the base where many British air force personnel and their families live along with some Germans.
The bomb alarm was raised after a dog trained by the British to detect explosives barked on inspecting the car.
Police said around 300 and 400 people who had been evacuated from a 200-metre (yards) radius around the car could return home.

Security at British bases has been high since the Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrilla force, which opposes British rule of Northern Ireland, ended a 17-month truce last year by bombing targets in Britain and a base in Germany last June.
Peace talks resumed on Tuesday in the Northern Ireland capital Belfast after a three-month break due to last month's British general election.

Sinn Fein, the political wing of the IRA, are not being included in the talks because the IRA has failed to declare a new ceasefire. Its last ceasefire ended in February 1996 with a wave of bomb atttacks in London.
